items.text: Many women in the UK are visiting new places called rage room s. In these rooms, people use hammers to break old TVs, plates, and boxes. People go there because they feel very stressed , tired, or sad about life and work. Owners of these rooms say that most of their visitors are women. Doctors say that it is good to let out bad feelings in a safe space. Men can get angry during sports, but women must be quiet and calm. Breaking things makes people feel happy and strong for a short time. But it cannot solve big life problems forever. Difficult words: hammer (a hand tool which we use for breaking things), stressed (worried and upset), owner (a person who has something and it belongs to him or her). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Rage rooms are becoming very popular in the UK, especially for women. In these special rooms, people pay to break things like old TVs, plates, and glasses with big hammers. About 75 percent of the customers are women who are trying to deal with work stress, busy family lives, or deep sadness after losing loved ones. Experts explain that society usually expects women to stay calm, so they don’t have many places to express anger. Smashing things gives people a quick feeling of power and release. On the other hand, doctors say that while rage rooms are fun and help you feel better for a short time, breaking things doesn’t fix big emotional problems forever. Difficult words: rage (uncontrollable anger), sadness (when you are sad), smash (to break something into pieces with great force). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Across the UK, a growing number of people, especially women, are turning to so-called rage rooms to destroy everyday items like flat-screen televisions and crockery with mallets and hammers. Owners report that up to three-quarters of their customers are female. Many use the sessions to cope with everyday stress, child-rearing pressures, or deep emotional trauma such as bereavement . Psychologists note that societal expectations often force women to suppress anger, unlike sports events where men are traditionally permitted to shout freely. Inside a rage room, participants find a safe, controlled environment where they can express frustration without judgment . While smashing objects provides an immediate surge of adrenaline and physical relief, experts caution that it doesn’t serve as a permanent therapeutic cure for long-term psychological problems. Instead, they view it as a helpful short-term release of energy, and advise individuals dealing with deep-seated emotional pain to seek professional long-term support. Difficult words: bereavement (suffering the loss of a loved one through death), suppress (to forcibly hold back, control, or prevent the expression of a feeling), judgment (an opinion or decision formed after thought or legal process). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Many kids love playing with squishy toys. Scientists test some of these toys to see if they are safe. They find that one toy has too much of one chemical. This chemical can hurt children. Also, if squishies stay in a hot car for a long time, they can break. Hot liquid may come out. This can hurt a child’s skin. The store takes the bad toy away. They give money back to parents. Experts tell families to check toy labels and keep the toys away from hot places like cars. Difficult words: squishy (soft, not hard when you touch it), liquid (a substance which flows, like water or gel), label (a piece of paper on a product which gives information about it). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Squishy toys are very popular with children who love to collect and squeeze them. But reports from around the world show that some of these toys may not be safe. A team in Singapore tested 18 squishy toys in a laboratory to check for dangerous chemicals. They found that most toys were fine, but one pink toy had high levels of a chemical called DINP, which is used to make plastic soft. This chemical was higher than local safety limits and can be harmful to children’s health. Tests also showed that if squishies are left in a hot car, they can get very hot, break, and leak dangerous liquid. After finding these results, the store removed the unsafe toy and offered refunds to customers. Difficult words: squishy (a soft toy), safety limit (the maximum amount of a chemical in a product to be still safe), refund (money given back to a customer who returns an unsafe or unwanted product). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Squishy toys have become extremely popular among children, who collect and squeeze them for stress relief. However, international safety concerns have prompted investigations into what these toys contain. Researchers and journalists tested 18 different squishies in Singapore for harmful chemicals like benzene and phthalates that are linked to cancer, hormone disruption , and developmental risks. While no benzene was detected, laboratory testing revealed that several toys contained restricted plasticisers . One pink toy exceeded Singapore’s legal limit by 1.7 times. Experts warn that prolonged heat, such as being left inside a parked car, can cause these toys to soften, leak, or rupture under pressure, and potentially cause skin irritation or burns. Following the findings, the affected retailer pulled the unsafe product from its shelves and offered customers refunds. Authorities advise parents to inspect toy labels carefully, avoid leaving them in direct sunlight, and monitor children during play. Difficult words: phthalate (a chemical additive that makes plastics softer, more flexible, and resilient), hormone disruption (an interference with the hormones, which can affect growth and health), plasticiser (a chemical substance added to materials to increase their softness, flexibility, or stretchiness). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Nvidia is a big tech company. Its boss, Jensen Huang, leaves his job suddenly . The company’s stock price falls. Huang leaves after news about his relationship with a woman who may be a spy for China. Nvidia chooses another boss for some time. So the business stays safe. Experts say that it will be very hard to find a new leader. Huang is the boss for 33 years. Now, US officials want to check if Nvidia breaks any rules. The company sells computer parts to China. This big problem may make trade between the US and China more difficult. Difficult words: suddenly (quickly, without a plan), stock price (how much one part of a company costs), spy (a person who gets information about other people or countries and they do not know about it). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Nvidia’s share price dropped quickly after its CEO and co-founder, Jensen Huang, suddenly resigned. He left the company after facing serious investigations over a personal affair with a woman who was a suspected Chinese spy , as well as a second affair with a company manager. To keep business running smoothly, Nvidia named its finance boss as temporary leader. Experts say replacing Huang will be very difficult because he led the company for 33 years and was very important to its success in AI. US officials plan to investigate what the company knew about the spying and whether Nvidia broke rules by selling computer chips to China. This problem could lead to stricter US trade laws and increased tension between America and China. Difficult words: spy (a person secretly collecting and reporting sensitive information for a foreign government or competitor), temporary (when something lasts for only some time), tension (a state of difficult relations between countries or people). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Nvidia’s share price dropped sharply after its co-founder and longtime boss, Jensen Huang, suddenly resigned. His decision followed growing pressure and a company investigation into his secret relationship with a woman suspected of spying for China. Media reports also revealed a second affair with an executive inside Nvidia. To keep the business stable during this difficult change, the company appointed its finance chief as interim CEO to reassure investors and maintain stability during the unexpected leadership change. However, business experts warn that replacing Huang will be very hard, because he led Nvidia for 33 years and had no clear plan for a successor . Beyond problems inside the company, the scandal raises serious questions about whether Nvidia broke US rules by selling advanced computer chips to China. Experts expect US politicians and police to investigate the company closely. They warn that Nvidia’s weaker influence in Washington could lead to stricter trade limits and increase political tension between the US and China. Difficult words: executive (a person with senior managerial responsibility in a business organization), interim (temporary), successor (a person who takes over a job, office, or position after someone else leaves). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A big computer problem at Microsoft stops many services around the world on Friday. People cannot use Outlook email, Teams, or other work apps for hours. Microsoft says that its main computers have too much work. They stop working. But it is not an attack by hackers. The company starts slowly fixing the problem. Technology experts say that companies should not use only one big tech company for everything. If one system breaks, people cannot do their jobs. Businesses need good backup plans so they can keep working when a problem comes. Difficult words: main (the biggest or most important thing), fix (to repair), backup (an extra copy of data or a plan for a situation when something stops working). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A huge Microsoft system failure on Friday the 13th stopped important services like Outlook, Teams, and Microsoft 365 from working around the world. More than 130,000 people reported problems with Outlook, and thousands couldn’t send emails or join online meetings. Microsoft said its computer servers got overloaded and stopped responding, though it confirmed this was not a cyberattack. The company slowly started fixing the problem to bring services back online. A technology expert explained that this crash shows the danger of businesses depending on just one tech company for all their daily work. He advised companies to use more than one provider and build strong backup plans so that one computer crash doesn’t stop their whole business from operating. Difficult words: failure (when something stops working properly), overloaded (given too much work, data, or weight to handle properly), failure (when something stops working properly). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A major global Microsoft outage on Friday the 13th disrupted essential services for hundreds of thousands of users worldwide and affected Outlook, Teams, Microsoft 365, OneDrive, and Copilot. At the peak of the disruption, a monitoring website recorded over 130,000 reports for Outlook and 46,000 for Microsoft 365. Microsoft said a core process on its servers became overwhelmed and stopped responding, but ruled out a cyberattack and began a gradual recovery. A cybersecurity expert noted that the incident highlights the serious risks of businesses relying on a single technology provider for daily operations. When major cloud platforms fail, companies can lose access to emails, online meetings, and security verification codes, which brings daily work to a standstill . Experts advise organizations not to put all their eggs in one basket, and urge them to diversify their digital providers and prepare strong backup plans to stay resilient during future technical crashes. Difficult words: rule out (to eliminate or exclude something as a possibility or cause), standstill (a situation in which all movement, activity, or work has stopped completely), resilient (able to withstand or recover quickly from difficult conditions, shocks, or system failures). You can watch the video news lower on this page.
